content:
Proofs of the Obligations in obligations.txt

Method: natural deduction, numbered lines, justifications in brackets.
Subproofs are indented; discharged assumptions appear in [square
brackets] at the line where they are introduced.

Notation (as in semantics.txt): e --> e' single step, e -->* e'
multi-step, s(n) successor, v value (literal), mu(e) = number of
operators (abs, +, -) in e, [[e]] denotation (Sec. 6 of
semantics.txt), P1-P3 the properties of spec.txt.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
0. BACKGROUND ARITHMETIC FACTS (admitted)

The following are standard theorems of Peano arithmetic / the ordered
ring Z. They are admitted here to keep the development focused on
the semantics; they are not obligations of this development and none
of them is an open problem.

  A1  (sign partition)   Every n in Z is exactly one of:
                          0,  s(m) with m >= 0,  -s(m) with m >= 0.
                         The three classes are pairwise disjoint
                         (0 =/= s(m), 0 =/= -s(m), s(m) =/= -s(k)).

  A2  (successor positive)  m >= 0  implies  s(m) >= 0 (in fact > 0).

  A3  (inverse involution)  for m > 0:  -(-m) = m,
                         in particular -(-s(m)) = s(m).

  A4  (injectivity)      s(m) = s(k) => m = k,
                         -s(m) = -s(k) => m = k.

  A5  (decidable signs)  for each n:  n >= 0  or  n < 0  (exactly one,
                         by A1); hence "n >= 0" is decidable.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
L1. LEMMA: values do not step
    Claim: for every value v there is no e' with v --> e'.

    1. Let v be a value; v is a literal n in Z.            [Sec. 1]
    2. Suppose, for contradiction, v --> e'.               [assumption]
    3. The root rule of the derivation of 2 is one of the nine rules
       of semantics.txt Sec. 3.                            [inversion]
    4. The source expression of each rule is respectively:
       e1+e2, v1+e2, e1-e2, v1-e2, abs(e), abs(0), abs(s(n)),
       abs(-s(n)), n1+n2, n1-n2.                    [inspection, Sec. 3]
    5. None of these is a bare literal.                    [4, syntax]
    6. Contradiction with 2.                        [2,3,4,5, ⊥-intro]
    7. Therefore no e' with v --> e'.            [6, discharge 2, ⊥-elim]

    ∎ L1

L2. LEMMA: single-step soundness (used in O9; proves O9.1, O9.2)
    Claim: for all e, e':  e --> e'  implies  [[e]] = [[e']].

    Proof by induction on the derivation of e --> e'.

    1. Computation rules (direct verification):
       1.1 S-AbsZero: e = abs(0), e' = 0.
           [[abs(0)]] = |[[0]]| = |0| = 0 = [[0]].
           (|0| = 0 because 0 >= 0 and P2.)        [def [[·]], P2, A1]
       1.2 S-AbsPos: e = abs(s(n)), e' = s(n), side condition n >= 0.
           [[abs(s(n))]] = |s(n)| = s(n) = [[s(n)]].
           (|s(n)| = s(n) because s(n) >= 0 by A2 and P2.)
                                                            [def, A2, P2]
       1.3 S-AbsNeg: e = abs(-s(n)), e' = s(n), side condition n >= 0.
           [[abs(-s(n))]] = |-s(n)| = s(n) = [[s(n)]].
           (-s(n) < 0 by A1; P3 gives |-s(n)| = -(-s(n)); A3 gives
           -(-s(n)) = s(n).)                               [def, A1, P3, A3]
       1.4 S-Plus: e = n1 + n2, e' = (n1+n2).
           [[n1 + n2]] = [[n1]] + [[n2]] = n1 + n2 = [[(n1+n2)]].
                                            [def [[·]]; notation of Sec. 2]
       1.5 S-Minus: symmetric to 1.4.                              [1.4]
    2. Congruence rules:
       2.1 S-Abs: e = abs(e0), e' = abs(e0'), premise e0 --> e0'.
           IH: [[e0]] = [[e0']].
           [[abs(e0)]] = |[[e0]]| = |[[e0']]| = [[abs(e0')]].  [IH, def [[·]]]
       2.2 S-PlusLeft: e = a + b, e' = a' + b, premise a --> a'.
           IH: [[a]] = [[a']].
           [[a + b]] = [[a]] + [[b]] = [[a']] + [[b]] = [[a' + b]].
                                                              [IH, def]
       2.3 S-PlusRight, S-MinusLeft, S-MinusRight: symmetric.      [2.2]
    3. Every derivation is a computation rule (case 1) or a
       congruence rule (case 2).                          [Sec. 3]
    4. Therefore [[e]] = [[e']] in all cases.        [1,2,3, ∨-elim]

    ∎ L2

L3. LEMMA: uniqueness of normal forms (used in O7, M.2)
    Claim: e -->* v and e -->* w with v, w values  implies  v = w.

    Proof by induction on the number k of steps in the first chain.

    1. k = 0: e = v. The second chain is v -->* w.
       1.1 If it has 0 steps, w = v. Done.                 [S-Refl only]
       1.2 If it has >= 1 step it begins with v --> e0, but values do
           not step (L1). Contradiction; so 1.1 applies.  [L1, ⊥-elim]
    2. k+1: the first chain is e --> e0 -->* v (k steps after the
       first). The second chain e -->* w:
       2.1 If it has 0 steps, e = w is a value; but e --> e0 steps,
           contradicting L1. Hence it has >= 1 step.      [L1, ⊥-elim]
       2.2 So the second chain begins e --> e0' -->* w.
       2.3 e --> e0 and e --> e0', so e0 = e0'.                  [O2]
       2.4 e0 -->* v and e0 -->* w with v, w values; the chains have
           k steps. IH: v = w.                               [IH, 2.4]
    3. Therefore v = w in all cases.                    [1,2, ∨-elim]

    ∎ L3

---------------------------------------------------------------------
O1. step-relation-well-defined

    Claim: --> is well-defined; each rule is well-formed, side
    conditions satisfiable and decidable, notation unambiguous.

    1. For each of the nine rules, the premises are either
       judgements e --> e' or side conditions "v value" / "n >= 0",
       and the conclusion is a judgement e --> e' with e, e'
       belonging to the grammar of Sec. 1.         [inspection, Sec. 3]
       1.1 Congruence rules: the conclusion places the premise's
           expressions back into the same context; the grammar is
           closed under abs(.), .+., .-.            [1, grammar closure]
       1.2 S-AbsZero: abs(0), 0 in grammar.                       [1]
       1.3 S-AbsPos/S-AbsNeg: abs(s(n)), s(n), abs(-s(n)) in
           grammar for n >= 0.                                    [1]
       1.4 S-Plus/S-Minus: sources n1 + n2, n1 - n2 and targets
           (n1+n2), (n1-n2) are literals, hence in grammar.       [1]
    2. Side conditions are satisfiable: n = 0 satisfies n >= 0 in
       S-AbsPos and S-AbsNeg.                              [A1, witness 0]
    3. Side conditions are decidable: by A5 exactly one of n >= 0,
       n < 0 holds, effectively.                               [A5]
    4. The notation denotes uniquely:
       4.1 s(n) is the unique successor of n, -s(n) its unique
           additive inverse.                              [A4, field axioms]
       4.2 (n1+n2) and (n1-n2) are unique: + and - are total
           functions on Z.                              [arithmetic of Z]
    5. Hence --> is a well-defined relation on expressions.
                                                       [1-4, ∧-intro]

    ∎ O1  (subsumes O1.1-O1.3)

O2. step-determinism

    Claim: for all e, e1, e2: e --> e1 and e --> e2  implies  e1 = e2.

    Proof by structural induction on e.

     1. Let e, e1, e2 with (I) e --> e1 and (II) e --> e2.
                                                     [assumptions, for →-intro]
     2. Case e is a literal (value):
        2.1 v --> e1 would contradict L1.               [I, L1, ⊥-elim]
        3. Case closed vacuously.
     4. Case e = abs(e0):
        4.1 Sub-case e0 is a value:
            4.1.1 e0 is exactly one of 0, s(n), -s(n).      [A1]
            4.1.2 S-Abs is inapplicable: its premise e0 --> e0'
                  is unsatisfiable since values do not step. [L1]
            4.1.3 If e0 = 0: only S-AbsZero matches (the sources
                  abs(0), abs(s(n)), abs(-s(n)) are pairwise
                  distinct by A1, and congruences are excluded by
                  4.1.2). e1 = 0; likewise e2 = 0. So e1 = e2.
                                                   [I, II, 4.1.2, A1, =-intro]
            4.1.4 If e0 = s(n): only S-AbsPos matches; e1 = s(n) = e2.
                                                                     [4.1.3]
            4.1.5 If e0 = -s(n): only S-AbsNeg; e1 = s(n) = e2.      [4.1.3]
        4.2 Sub-case e0 is not a value:
            4.2.1 S-AbsZero/Pos/Neg are inapplicable: their sources
                  are abs(value), but e0 is not 0, s(n), or -s(n)
                  (else it would be a value).                       [A1]
            4.2.2 Only S-Abs matches (I) and (II): e1 = abs(e0'),
                  e2 = abs(e0'') with e0 --> e0' and e0 --> e0''.    [I, II]
            4.2.3 e0' = e0''.                    [IH on e0, 4.2.2, O2-form]
            4.2.4 e1 = abs(e0') = abs(e0'') = e2.           [4.2.2, 4.2.3]
     5. Case e = a + b:
        5.1 a not a value: only S-PlusLeft matches (S-Plus needs
            both operands values; S-PlusRight needs a value).
            e1 = a' + b, e2 = a'' + b with a --> a', a --> a'';
            IH on a: a' = a''; hence e1 = e2.                [I, II, IH]
        5.2 a value, b not a value: only S-PlusRight matches (L1
            blocks S-PlusLeft); e1 = a + b', e2 = a + b''; IH on b:
            b' = b''; e1 = e2.                            [I, II, L1, IH]
        5.3 a, b values: only S-Plus matches (congruences blocked by
            L1); e1 = (a+b) = e2.                          [I, II, L1]
     6. Case e = a - b: symmetric to 5 with S-MinusLeft, S-MinusRight,
        S-Minus.                                                  [5]
     7. In every case e1 = e2.                    [3,4,5,6, ∨-elim]
     8. Therefore for all e, e1, e2: (e --> e1 ∧ e --> e2) → e1 = e2.
                                              [7, discharge 1, ∀-intro]

    ∎ O2  (subsumes O2.1-O2.3; note 4.1.3 and 5 establish O2.2's
      no-overlap claim explicitly)

O3. progress

    Claim: for every expression e: value(e) or there is e' with
    e --> e'.

    Proof by structural induction on e.

     1. Case e = n (literal): value(e). Left disjunct.        [Sec. 1]
     2. Case e = abs(e0):
        2.1 IH: value(e0) or e0 --> e0' for some e0'.
        2.2 If e0 --> e0': S-Abs gives abs(e0) --> abs(e0'). Right
            disjunct.                                           [S-Abs]
        2.3 If value(e0): e0 is 0, s(n), or -s(n).              [A1]
            2.3.1 e0 = 0:   S-AbsZero: abs(0) --> 0.            [S-AbsZero]
            2.3.2 e0 = s(n): S-AbsPos: abs(s(n)) --> s(n).      [S-AbsPos]
            2.3.3 e0 = -s(n): S-AbsNeg: abs(-s(n)) --> s(n).    [S-AbsNeg]
            2.3.4 Right disjunct in all sub-cases.        [2.3, ∨-elim]
     3. Case e = a + b:
        3.1 IH on a and on b.
        3.2 a --> a': S-PlusLeft: a + b --> a' + b.      [S-PlusLeft]
        3.3 value(a) and b --> b': S-PlusRight (premise "v1 value"
            met): a + b --> a + b'.                          [S-PlusRight]
        3.4 value(a), value(b): S-Plus: a + b --> (a+b).          [S-Plus]
        3.5 Right disjunct in all cases.                  [3.2-3.4, ∨-elim]
     4. Case e = a - b: symmetric with S-MinusLeft, S-MinusRight,
        S-Minus.                                                  [3]
     5. Therefore value(e) or e steps, for all e.      [1-4, ∨-elim]

    ∎ O3  (subsumes O3.1-O3.3)

O4. termination

    Claim: every expression e reduces to a value, and every reduction
    sequence from e is finite.

    Lemma T1: for every step e --> e':  mu(e') <= mu(e) - 1.
    Proof by induction on the derivation of e --> e'.
      1. Computation rules (S-AbsZero, S-AbsPos, S-AbsNeg, S-Plus,
         S-Minus): the source is exactly one operator applied to
         values; the target is a literal. mu(source) = 1,
         mu(target) = 0. Decrease = 1.                    [def mu, Sec. 3]
      2. Congruence rules (S-PlusLeft/Right, S-MinusLeft/Right,
         S-Abs): source = C[e0], target = C[e0'] with premise
         e0 --> e0'. The context C contributes the same operators to
         both sides, so
            mu(target) - mu(source) = mu(e0') - mu(e0) <= -1
         by the IH.                                [IH, def mu, arithmetic]
      3. Hence every step decreases mu by at least 1.   [1,2, ∨-elim]
    ∎ T1
    (Note: T1 strengthens the decomposition item O4.2 — congruence
    rules preserve the operator count of their own context and
    propagate the decrease of their premise; the induction makes
    this precise.)

    Main argument:
     1. mu(e) >= 0 for every e (a count of operators).          [O4.1]
     2. Along any chain e = e0 --> e1 --> ... --> ek, mu drops by at
        least 1 per step (T1), and mu >= 0 throughout.   [T1, 1]
     3. Hence k <= mu(e): every chain from e is finite.   [2, pigeonhole]
     4. A maximal chain from e must end in an expression f that
        admits no step; by O3, any non-value admits a step, so f is
        a value v.                                       [O3, contraposition]
     5. Therefore e -->* v with v a value, and all chains are finite.
                                                          [3,4, ∧-intro]

    ∎ O4  (subsumes O4.1-O4.4)

O5. abs-non-negative-case      (discharges P2 of spec.txt)

    Claim: for all x in Z: x >= 0  implies  abs(x) -->* x.

     1. Let x with x >= 0.                             [assumption]
     2. x = 0 or x = s(n) with n >= 0.                       [A1, 1]
     3. Case x = 0:
        3.1 abs(0) --> 0.                                [S-AbsZero]
        3.2 abs(0) -->* 0.                    [3.1, S-Refl, S-Trans]
        3.3 abs(x) -->* x (x = 0).                       [3.2, =-subst]
     4. Case x = s(n), n >= 0:
        4.1 abs(s(n)) --> s(n).        [S-AbsPos, side condition met]
        4.2 abs(s(n)) -->* s(n).              [4.1, S-Refl, S-Trans]
        4.3 abs(x) -->* x.                               [4.2, =-subst]
     5. abs(x) -->* x in both cases.               [3,4, ∨-elim]
     6. For all x: x >= 0 => abs(x) -->* x.   [5, discharge 1, ∀-intro]

    ∎ O5  (subsumes O5.1-O5.3)

O6. abs-negative-case          (discharges P3 of spec.txt)

    Claim: for all x in Z: x < 0  implies  abs(x) -->* -x.

     1. Let x with x < 0.                              [assumption]
     2. x = -s(n) with n >= 0, and n is unique.              [A1, A4]
     3. abs(-s(n)) --> s(n).        [S-AbsNeg, side condition met]
     4. abs(x) -->* s(n).                       [3, S-Refl, S-Trans]
     5. -x = -(-s(n)) = s(n).
        (-x = s(n) > 0, so A3 applies to m = -x.)          [2, A3, =-intro]
     6. abs(x) -->* -x.                                  [4, 5, =-subst]
     7. For all x: x < 0 => abs(x) -->* -x.   [6, discharge 1, ∀-intro]

    ∎ O6  (subsumes O6.1-O6.4; O6.1 = line 2, O6.2 = 3-4,
      O6.3 = line 5, O6.4 = line 6)

O7. result-non-negative        (discharges P1 of spec.txt)

    Claim: for all x, v: abs(x) -->* v  implies  v >= 0.

     1. Let x, v with abs(x) -->* v.                   [assumption]
     2. There is y with abs(x) -->* y and value(y).          [O4, O3]
     3. v = y.                                    [1, 2, L3 (NFU)]
     4. Case x >= 0:
        4.1 abs(x) -->* x and x is a value.                  [O5]
        4.2 y = x.                              [2, 4.1, L3 (NFU)]
        4.3 v = x >= 0.                               [3, 4.2, 1, A5]
     5. Case x < 0:
        5.1 abs(x) -->* -x and -x is a value.                [O6]
        5.2 -x = s(n) for some n >= 0.                       [A1, A3]
        5.3 y = -x = s(n).                      [2, 5.1, L3 (NFU)]
        5.4 v = s(n) >= 0.                          [3, 5.3, A2]
     6. v >= 0 in both cases.                     [4,5, A5, ∨-elim]
     7. For all x, v: abs(x) -->* v => v >= 0. [6, discharge 1, ∀-intro]

    ∎ O7  (subsumes O7.1-O7.3; O7.1 = lines 2-3 via L3,
      O7.2 = 4.3, O7.3 = 5.4)

O8. spec-characterization-uniqueness

    Claim: if y1 and y2 both satisfy P1-P3 of spec.txt for the same
    x, then y1 = y2.

     1. Let y1, y2 satisfy P1-P3 for x.                [assumption]
     2. x >= 0 or x < 0.                                     [A5]
     3. Case x >= 0:
        3.1 P2 (for y1): y1 = x.                        [1, P2, 3]
        3.2 P2 (for y2): y2 = x.                        [1, P2, 3]
        3.3 y1 = x = y2.                         [3.1, 3.2, =-trans]
     4. Case x < 0:
        4.1 P3 (for y1): y1 = -x.                       [1, P3, 4]
        4.2 P3 (for y2): y2 = -x.                       [1, P3, 4]
        4.3 y1 = -x = y2.                        [4.1, 4.2, =-trans]
     5. y1 = y2 in both cases.                    [3,4, ∨-elim]
     6. For all x, y1, y2: (P1-P3 for both) => y1 = y2.
                                              [5, discharge 1, ∀-intro]

    ∎ O8  (subsumes O8.1-O8.3)
    Remark: P2 and P3 alone already force uniqueness; P1 is needed
    only for the existence direction (it is satisfied by the value
    the semantics produces, see O7). This matches obligations.txt,
    where O7 carries P1.

O9. denotational-soundness     (Sec. 6 of semantics.txt)

    Claim: for all e, v:  e -->* v  implies  [[e]] = v.

    Proof by induction on the number k of steps in e -->* v.

     1. k = 0: e = v and v is a literal n. [[e]] = [[n]] = n = v.
                                                            [def [[·]]]
     2. k+1: e --> e0 -->* v (k steps after the first).
        2.1 [[e]] = [[e0]].                          [L2, single step]
        2.2 [[e0]] = v.                     [IH on the k-step tail]
        2.3 [[e]] = v.                            [2.1, 2.2, =-trans]
     3. Therefore for all e, v: e -->* v => [[e]] = v.
                                              [1,2, induction, ∀-intro]

    ∎ O9  (O9.1 = L2 case 1; O9.2 = L2 case 2; O9.3 = the induction
      above, with L2 supplying the one-step base)

---------------------------------------------------------------------
MAIN THEOREM     (M.1-M.6 of obligations.txt)

    Theorem T: for every x in Z there is a value y with
      (a) abs(x) -->* y,
      (b) y = x   if x >= 0,
      (c) y = -x  if x < 0,
      (d) y >= 0,
    and y is the unique value satisfying (a)-(d); moreover y = |x|
    as specified by spec.txt, and the semantics agrees with the
    denotation on all expressions.

     1. Let x in Z.                                    [assumption]
     2. Existence: there is y with abs(x) -->* y and value(y).
                                                       [O4, O3  (M.1)]
     3. Uniqueness of the computed value: if abs(x) -->* y1 and
        abs(x) -->* y2 with y1, y2 values, then y1 = y2.
                                              [O2, O4, L3  (M.2)]
     4. P2 holds: if x >= 0 then y = x.
            4.1 abs(x) -->* x (x a value).                  [O5]
            4.2 y = x.                                [2, 4.1, L3]
                                                        [O5  (M.3a)]
     5. P3 holds: if x < 0 then y = -x.
            5.1 abs(x) -->* -x (-x a value, by A1/A3).      [O6]
            5.2 y = -x.                               [2, 5.1, L3]
                                                        [O6  (M.3b)]
     6. P1 holds: y >= 0.                          [2, O7  (M.4)]
     7. y is the unique value with y >= 0, y = x (x >= 0),
        y = -x (x < 0), i.e. y = |x| as specified in spec.txt.
                                            [O8, 4, 5, 6  (M.5)]
     8. Agreement with the denotation: for all e, v, e -->* v implies
        [[e]] = v; in particular [[abs(x)]] = y.               [O9 (M.6)]
     9. Statements (a)-(d) hold for all x, uniquely.
                                        [2-8, discharge 1, ∀-intro]

    ∎ T

---------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS SUMMARY

  O1  step-relation-well-defined ............. discharged (proof O1)
  O2  step-determinism ....................... discharged (proof O2)
  O3  progress ............................... discharged (proof O3)
  O4  termination ............................ discharged (T1 + proof O4)
  O5  abs-non-negative-case .................. discharged (proof O5)
  O6  abs-negative-case ...................... discharged (proof O6)
  O7  result-non-negative .................... discharged (L3 + proof O7)
  O8  spec-characterization-uniqueness ....... discharged (proof O8)
  O9  denotational-soundness ................. discharged (L2 + proof O9)
  T   main-theorem ........................... discharged (proof T)

  No obligation is open.

  External assumptions: the admitted background arithmetic facts
  A1-A5 of Sec. 0 (sign partition of Z, successor positivity,
  inverse involution, injectivity, decidable signs). These are
  standard theorems of Peano arithmetic over Z, not open problems;
  they are the only assumptions used beyond the definitions of
  spec.txt and semantics.txt. If one insists on full self-
  containment, formalizing A1-A5 inside Peano arithmetic is routine
  and is the only remaining (mechanical, non-essential) gap.
